guard_patterns.handling: Require a directly accessible official source.
Keep provisional and final estimates distinct.
Keep CO2, CH4, N2O and fluorinated gases distinct.
Keep LULUCF emissions/removals and non-LULUCF emissions explicit.
Preserve CCA scheme phase, facility scope and target period.
Keep model assumptions and scenario outputs distinct from observations.
Keep heat, energy, rail activity and payments distinct from GHG emissions.
Preserve calendar, financial-year and quarterly reference periods.
No parcel value without geometry, identity, activity and method binding.
Require deterministic PASS review for every control.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 provisional sector-scope QA
facts: The 2025 publication is provisional rather than final.
It provides an early estimate for the latest full calendar year.
It is based on provisional inland energy statistics from Energy Trends.
Territorial Emissions Statistics sectors are broad reporting sectors.
Electricity supply is a distinct sector.
Fuel supply is a distinct sector.
Domestic transport is a distinct sector.
Buildings and product uses are a distinct sector.
Industry, agriculture, waste and LULUCF remain distinct sectors.
Broad national sectors are not parcel emissions measurements.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 provisional fuel-scope QA
facts: The provisional release allocates emissions into broad fuel classifications.
Gas is a distinct fuel classification.
Oil is a distinct fuel classification.
Coal is a distinct fuel classification.
Other solid fuels are distinct from coal.
Other emissions are reported separately from the major fuel classes.
Fuel classification is not the same as economic-sector classification.
Fuel activity inputs can be revised before final inventory publication.
Fuel totals require consistent inventory methods for comparison.
Fuel-class statistics do not identify a parcel source without local binding.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 provisional revision guard QA
facts: The 2025 estimates are explicitly subject to revision.
Final estimates replace the early provisional view when available.
Provisional estimates provide an early indication rather than final inventory values.
The release is Accredited Official Statistics.
Reference year 2025 must remain attached to these estimates.
Provisional status must be retained in downstream provenance.
A later final value must not be silently backfilled into a provisional record.
Changes between provisional and final estimates can reflect improved source data.
Comparisons should use consistent publication status where possible.
Revision status does not create parcel-level evidence.

packages.title: DESNZ 2024 final SIC update timing QA
facts: Final UK territorial greenhouse-gas estimates cover 1990 to 2024.
Final estimates are presented by source.
End-user estimates are added in a later update stage.
SIC-based estimates are added in June.
The 2024 final publication was updated on 25 June 2026.
Source, end-user and SIC views are different allocations of the inventory.
SIC allocation should not be treated as a physical point-source map.
Final status is different from the 2025 provisional release.
Historic series can be revised when inventory methods improve.
National final statistics remain above parcel measurement level.

packages.title: Annual statement gas-species 2024 QA
facts: The 2024 annual statement reports emissions by greenhouse-gas species.
Carbon dioxide is reported separately.
Methane is reported separately.
Nitrous oxide is reported separately.
Hydrofluorocarbons are reported separately.
Perfluorocarbons are reported separately.
Sulphur hexafluoride is reported separately.
Gas-specific values are expressed on a CO2-equivalent basis where appropriate.
Gas totals should not be substituted for one another.
Gas-species national totals are not parcel measurements.

packages.title: Annual statement LULUCF net-boundary QA
facts: The annual statement distinguishes emissions excluding LULUCF.
It separately reports net LULUCF emissions or removals.
It also reports net emissions or removals including net LULUCF.
A removal can offset emissions in a net national total.
Gross non-LULUCF emissions and net totals are different accounting boundaries.
LULUCF treatment must be explicit when comparing totals.
Net national accounting does not mean every land parcel is a net sink.
Land-sector values require land-use-specific methods.
A national removal cannot be distributed uniformly across land.
Parcel attribution requires verified local land-use geometry and method.

packages.title: Annual statement fluorinated-gas separation QA
facts: Hydrofluorocarbons are separate inventory gases.
Perfluorocarbons are separate inventory gases.
Sulphur hexafluoride is a separate inventory gas.
Fluorinated gases should not be merged with methane without explicit CO2e aggregation.
Gas-specific trends can differ from total GHG trends.
Inventory gas identity is part of provenance.
A CO2e total does not erase the underlying gas species.
Product-use emissions can involve fluorinated gases.
National gas totals do not identify equipment or facility location.
Parcel-level attribution requires a verified emitting activity and geometry.

packages.title: NAEI 2026 inventory-product vintage QA
facts: NAEI lists the 2026 UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory for 1990 to 2024.
The 2026 source pivot table is a distinct data product.
Country inventories for England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are separate products.
Point-source data have their own publication vintage.
Gridded data have their own publication vintage.
Interactive emissions maps have their own publication vintage.
Local-authority maps have their own publication vintage.
Not every NAEI product is updated on the same date.
Dataset vintage must be preserved during joins.
A map or grid product is not automatically a cadastral parcel measurement.

packages.title: DESNZ local peatland gas-boundary QA
facts: Local GHG estimates spatially disaggregate the national inventory.
The local methodology includes LULUCF emissions and removals.
Peatlands can emit greenhouse gases depending on condition and management.
Undrained modified peatlands are distinguished in the methodology.
Rewetted peatlands are distinguished in the methodology.
Near-natural peatlands are distinguished in the methodology.
Drainage ditches on peatlands can contribute emissions.
Wildfire and land conversion can contribute LULUCF emissions.
CO2, methane and nitrous oxide processes should remain distinct.
Local-authority spatial disaggregation is not parcel measurement.

packages.title: DESNZ LULUCF versus agriculture boundary QA
facts: The local technical report separates LULUCF from agriculture inventory treatment.
Non-CO2 emissions from agricultural land can be reported in the agriculture sector.
LULUCF includes land-use-change processes.
Nitrogen fertilisation of new forests can contribute N2O within LULUCF methodology.
Soil mineralisation following land-use change can contribute N2O.
Agricultural fertilisation emissions should not be silently moved into LULUCF.
Sector boundaries follow national inventory methodology.
End-user local estimates are spatial disaggregations rather than field measurements.
Land-use category is essential provenance.
Parcel attribution requires verified land-use and inventory-category binding.

packages.title: CCA 2026 TP7 facility-target boundary QA
facts: The new Climate Change Agreements scheme begins in 2026.
Target Period 7 runs from 1 January to 31 December 2026.
The new scheme uses facility-level targets.
Facility-level targets replace the previous bubbled multi-facility approach.
Eligibility remains tied to specified eligible activities.
Operators confirm eligibility for the new scheme.
Targets relate to energy efficiency or carbon-dioxide performance under the scheme.
CCA facility scope is a regulatory scheme boundary.
A CCA facility is not automatically identical to a cadastral parcel.
Parcel use requires verified facility-to-parcel geometry.

packages.title: CCA old/new scheme transition QA
facts: Previous CCA obligations can remain live during transition.
Certification Period 7 from the previous scheme has been extended to 30 June 2027.
The new 2026 scheme has separate target periods.
Old-scheme decisions and enforcement can remain governed by earlier guidance.
New-scheme eligibility and targets use the 2026 framework.
Old and new scheme records must not be silently merged.
Scheme phase is part of record provenance.
Target-period identifiers should be preserved.
Historic performance data may use the earlier bubbled structure.
Scheme transition does not create parcel emissions data.

packages.title: CCA 2026 target-period deadline QA
facts: Target Period 7 covers calendar year 2026.
The TP7 data submission deadline is 1 May 2027.
Target Period 8 covers 2027 and 2028.
The TP8 data submission deadline is 1 May 2029.
Target Period 9 covers 2029 and 2030.
The TP9 data submission deadline is 1 May 2031.
Target-period duration and report deadline are different dates.
CCA performance records should retain their target-period identity.
A submission deadline is not an emissions measurement date.
Parcel attribution remains outside the scheme reporting timetable itself.

packages.title: CCA historical target-unit performance scope QA
facts: Environment Agency publishes historical CCA target-unit performance data.
CCA participation is voluntary for eligible operators.
Participants can receive Climate Change Levy benefits when scheme conditions are met.
Historic operators reported energy consumption.
Historic operators reported carbon emissions.
Historic operators reported performance against targets.
Historical target units can group eligible activities according to the old scheme structure.
Historic target-unit data should not be assumed to follow 2026 facility-level structure.
Performance against a target is not the same as direct source measurement.
Parcel mapping requires independent facility and geometry evidence.

packages.title: CCA sector versus facility performance QA
facts: CCA reporting can be summarised at sector level.
Target-unit performance is a more specific reporting layer than sector totals.
The 2026 scheme moves target setting toward facility level.
Sector performance should not be assigned uniformly to facilities.
Facility performance should not be assigned uniformly to parcels.
Energy efficiency targets and carbon targets are related but distinct metrics.
Historic and current scheme structures should be identified explicitly.
Eligibility is process-based rather than cadastral.
Regulatory reporting boundaries can span multiple physical assets.
Parcel GHG remains unbound without spatial and activity evidence.

packages.title: Industrial energy-efficiency definition QA
facts: DESNZ published updated evidence on UK industrial energy-efficiency potential in March 2026.
The research defines energy efficiency in relation to delivered energy consumed per unit of industrial output.
Energy efficiency is not identical to total production reduction.
Energy efficiency potential is assessed across industrial processes.
Fuel switching is a separate decarbonisation lever.
Carbon capture utilisation and storage is a separate lever.
Energy efficiency can change energy demand without directly measuring site emissions.
Production output is part of the efficiency denominator concept.
Potential savings are analytical evidence rather than parcel measurements.
Parcel use requires site-specific baseline, output and geometry evidence.

packages.title: Industrial energy-efficiency process-only scope QA
facts: The 2026 industrial energy-efficiency research focuses on industrial processes.
Building-level efficiency measures are outside the stated research scope.
Behavioural efficiency measures are outside the stated research scope.
Process energy-efficiency opportunities should not be applied to building energy by default.
Industrial sectors have different process technologies.
Technology applicability can vary by industrial subsector.
Energy-efficiency potential is not a measured emissions inventory.
Scope exclusions must remain visible in downstream use.
A national industrial potential cannot be uniformly allocated to sites.
Parcel estimates require local process and site evidence.

packages.title: Industrial efficiency rebound-effect guard QA
facts: DESNZ published research on industrial energy and resource-efficiency rebound effects in March 2026.
A rebound effect can offset some expected efficiency-based savings.
Rebound can arise when efficiency induces increased consumption.
Expected technical savings and realised net savings are therefore different concepts.
Rebound analysis is relevant to policy appraisal.
Rebound analysis is relevant to carbon-abatement modelling.
A technical efficiency percentage should not be treated as guaranteed emissions reduction.
Behaviour after an intervention can affect realised outcomes.
Modelled rebound is not direct site emissions measurement.
Parcel-level impact requires observed site activity and a verified method.

packages.title: COMIT model-pathway versus observation QA
facts: DESNZ published refreshed industry technology modelling assumptions in June 2026.
COMIT is the Cost Optimisation Model for Industry Technologies.
COMIT finds lowest-cost pathways for meeting UK industry energy needs to 2050.
The model includes decarbonisation technologies.
The model includes baseline technologies and costs.
A least-cost pathway is a model result rather than an observed deployment record.
Technology costs are assumptions that can change by model vintage.
Scenario outputs should not be treated as measured emissions.
Model evidence can inform candidate technologies.
Parcel attribution requires observed site technology and activity data.

packages.title: COMIT assumption-version guard QA
facts: COMIT was formerly known as the Net Zero Industrial Pathways Model 2.
The June 2026 report refreshes modelling assumptions.
Model-name changes should be preserved in provenance.
Baseline technology assumptions are distinct from decarbonisation technology assumptions.
Cost assumptions are not emissions measurements.
Model inputs and outputs should retain version information.
A newer assumption set should not be silently mixed with an older scenario result.
Model pathways can extend to 2050.
Long-term scenario values are not current parcel measurements.
Site-level use requires separate real-world validation.

packages.title: Non-Domestic RHI installation/heat/payment boundary QA
facts: Ofgem publishes public Non-Domestic RHI statistics and reports.
Reports include approved renewable-heating installation counts.
Reports include technology types.
Reports include country-level installation information.
Reports include heat generated by approved installations.
Reports include payments made based on heat generated.
Installation count, installed capacity, heat generation and payment are different measures.
Scheme accreditation is not a greenhouse-gas measurement.
Heat generation does not directly equal avoided emissions without a counterfactual and factor method.
Parcel use requires installation identity and geometry binding.

packages.title: Non-Domestic RHI technology/country scope QA
facts: Non-Domestic RHI reporting distinguishes renewable heating technologies.
Reporting can distinguish installations by country.
Cumulative capacity is a separate metric from installation count.
Biomethane producers are separately identifiable in scheme reporting.
Scheme statistics are regularly updated.
Technology mix should not be treated as fuel consumption without supporting data.
Installed capacity does not equal heat produced in a given period.
Heat produced does not by itself equal GHG savings.
Country totals do not identify a cadastral parcel.
Parcel evidence requires installation-level identity and spatial matching.

packages.title: Domestic RHI scheme-year and closure guard QA
facts: Ofgem published the Domestic RHI annual report for April 2025 to March 2026 on 17 July 2026.
The report covers Scheme Year 12.
The Domestic RHI began in 2014.
The scheme promoted low-carbon domestic heating technologies.
Eligible technologies included air-source heat pumps.
Eligible technologies included ground-source heat pumps.
Biomass boilers and solar thermal systems were also eligible.
The scheme closed to new applicants on 31 March 2022.
Later scheme-year reports can therefore describe ongoing legacy payments and activity.
Scheme participation does not directly measure parcel emissions.

packages.title: Domestic RHI expected-heat versus emissions QA
facts: Domestic RHI participants could receive quarterly payments over seven years.
Payments relate to low-carbon heat their systems were expected to produce under scheme rules.
Expected heat is not synonymous with measured household greenhouse-gas emissions.
A heat-pump installation does not reveal household electricity consumption by itself.
A biomass installation does not reveal lifecycle emissions by itself.
Technology identity can support a building-energy candidate.
Scheme records follow household or installation eligibility rather than cadastral parcel boundaries.
Avoided emissions require a baseline heating counterfactual.
Operational emissions require actual energy use and compatible factors.
Parcel use requires property and geometry binding.

packages.title: ORR freight activity metric-separation QA
facts: ORR publishes quarterly freight rail usage and performance statistics.
The January to March 2026 release was published on 11 June 2026.
Freight moved is reported in net tonne kilometres.
Freight lifted is reported in tonnes.
Freight train kilometres are reported separately.
These three activity metrics measure different aspects of rail freight.
Activity statistics are not greenhouse-gas emissions by themselves.
Rail emissions require energy or fuel and emissions-factor evidence.
Quarterly rail activity cannot be assigned to a parcel without route or facility linkage.
Freight activity can support transport-context candidates only when scope is preserved.

packages.title: ORR freight publication-lag and validation QA
facts: ORR receives some freight operational data from Network Rail on a four-weekly basis.
Publication timing depends on data receipt.
ORR can delay publication while validity queries are resolved.
Some operational tables can take up to 15 working days after period end to update.
Financial-year quarter labels should be preserved.
Q4 corresponds to January to March in the ORR financial-year convention.
Some freight tables scheduled with the January to March 2026 release were delayed.
Publication lag is a data-quality and timebase constraint.
Delayed tables should not be inferred from other activity metrics.
Rail activity remains non-parcel evidence without spatial and emissions-method binding.
